rdf:Description.rdfs:label: contains assertion from
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity contains a statement of fact or a logical assertion (or a collection of such facts and/or assertions) originally present in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note:
Example: We think that to stand on the top of giants [X] is a valuable principle to follow for our own research.
This object property is designed to be used to relate a separate abstract, summary or nanopublication to the cited entity upon which it is based.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites as potential solution
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity cites the cited entity as providing or containing a possible solution to the issues being discussed.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: This risk could be avoided using the approach shown in [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: parodies
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity imitates the characteristic style or content of the cited entity for comic effect, usually without explicit citation.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We act as giants on the shoulders of dwarfs [X]!

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: derides
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity express derision for the cited entity, or for ideas or conclusions contained within it.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: The ideas published in [X] are incredibly stupid.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: has citation characterization
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The relation between a citation and its characterization made by using a CiTO citation characterization property.
rdf:Description.skos:note:
This usage involved [OWL2 punning](http://www.w3.org/TR/2009/WD-owl2-new-features-20090611/#F12:_Punning), whereby a CiTO object property, such as the aforementioned `cito:extends`, is used as the object of an OWL assertion.
In such cases of OWL punning, the CiTO object properties are simultaneously considered both as normal object properties and also as proper named individuals of the class `owl:Thing`.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: affilation self citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation in which at least one author from each of the citing and the cited entities is affiliated with the same academic institution.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Like the ancestor class `cito:Citation`, `cito:AffiliationSelfCitation` and its accompanying object properties `cito:hasCitingEntity`, `cito:hasCitedEntity` and `cito:hasCitationCharacterization` can be employed to reify direct citation statements made using the CiTO citation object property `cito:cites` or one of its sub-properties, accompanied by an additional statement using `cito:sharesAuthorInstitutionWith` for linking the citing paper and the cited paper.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: has cited entity
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation between a citation and the cited entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: documents
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity documents information about the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Herein we report in detail the complete set of ontological rules defined in the Overlapping Ontology [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites for information
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity cites the cited entity as a source of information on the subject under discussion.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: The grammar of Pascal was introduced in [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: Citation Typing Ontology (CiTO)
rdf:Description.dc:creator: David Shotton (http://orcid.org/0000-0001-5506-523X)
Silvio Peroni (http://orcid.org/0000-0003-0530-4305)
rdf:Description.dc:title: The Citation Typing Ontology (CiTO)
rdf:Description.dcterms:bibliographicCitation: Peroni, S., Shotton, D. (2012). FaBiO and CiTO: ontologies for describing bibliographic resources and citations. In Journal of Web Semantics, 17: 33-43. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.websem.2012.08.001. Open Access at: https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3198992

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: journal self citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation in which the citing and the cited entities are published in the same journal.
rdf:Description.skos:note:
Like the ancestor class `cito:Citation`, `cito:JournalSelfCitation` and its accompanying object properties `cito:hasCitingEntity`, `cito:hasCitedEntity` and `cito:hasCitationCharacterization` can be employed to reify direct citation statements made using the CiTO citation object property `cito:cites` or one of its sub-properties, accompanied by an additional statement using `cito:sharesJournalWith` for linking the citing paper and the cited paper.
Derived from the blog post "Journal self-citations are increasingly biased toward impact factor years" by Ludo Waltman and Caspar Chorus (https://www.cwts.nl/blog?article=n-q2x264).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: agrees with
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity agrees with statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We share Galileo's opinion: the Earth moves [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites as related
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity cites the cited entity as one that is related.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: An analysis similar to what we proposed here is presented in [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is credited by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity makes contributions that are acknowledged by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is extended by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents facts, ideas or understandings that are extended by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: ridicules
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity ridicules the cited entity or aspects of its contents.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Galileo said that the Earth "moves" [X]; really? And where is it going?

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited as source document by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited as being the entity from which the citing entity is derived, or about which the citing entity contains metadata.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: updates
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity updates statements, ideas, hypotheses or understanding presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Earth moves, said Galileo [X]; in addition, we can say now it moves very fast.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: discusses
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity discusses statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We now examine if Galileo is right when he writes [X] that the Earth moves.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: provides data for
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents data that are used in work described in the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: obtains support from
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity obtains intellectual or factual support from the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Our ideas were also shared by Doe et al. [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: qualifies
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity qualifies or places conditions or restrictions upon statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Galileo's masterpiece "Dialogo sopra i due massimi sistemi del mondo" [X] is formally a dialog and substantially a scientific pamphlet.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: has citation creation date
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The date on which the citation was created. This has the same numerical value as the publication date of the citing bibliographic resource, but is a property of the citation itself. When combined with the citation time span, it permits that citation to be located in history.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: extends
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity extends facts, ideas or understandings presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We add to Galileo's findings concerning the Earth [X] that also the Moon moves.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is qualified by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents statements, ideas or conclusions that are qualified or have conditions placed upon them by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: provides conclusions for
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents conclusions that are used in work described in the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: obtains background from
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity obtains background information from the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: There is a need for more observational studies and studies using narrative causation to describe the potential contribution of information in problem-solving and decision-making [X]; our work addresses these needs.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: has citing entity
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation between a citation and the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites as source document
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity cites the cited entity as being the entity from which the citing entity is derived, or about which the citing entity contains metadata.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Several sections of this work are based on our literature review of the topic published as journal article [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited as evidence by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited for providing factual evidence to the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited for information by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited as a source of information on the subject under discussion in the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited as related by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited as being related to the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: has reply from
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity evokes a reply from the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: uses method in
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity describes work that uses a method detailed in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We follow [X] in using design patterns for testing.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: credits
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity acknowledges contributions made by the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Galileo was the first to observe Jupiter's satellites [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: includes quotation from
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity includes one or more quotations from the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note:
A quotation is a repetition of what someone has said, and is presented "within quotation marks", for example:
On June 4th 1940, Winston Churchill made a speech on the radio that has since become famous, that included the words: " ... we shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields and in the streets, we shall fight in the hills; we shall never surrender ..."
Example: As Newton wrote in [X]: "We are like dwarfs standing on the shoulders of giants".

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is described by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is described by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is supported by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity receives intellectual or factual support from the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: uses conclusions from
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity describes work that uses conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Building upon Galileo's findings [X], we discovered that all the planets move.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is discussed by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents statements, ideas or conclusions that are discussed by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: provides excerpt for
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity contains information, usually of a textual nature, that is excerpted by (used as an excerpt within) the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is confirmed by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents facts, ideas or statements that are confirmed by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: situation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A view on a set of entities. It can be seen as a "relational context", reifying a relation.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: self citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation in which the citing and the cited entities have something significant in common with one another, over and beyond their subject matter, for example authors, journal, institutional affiliation, or funding agency.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: provides assertion for
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity contains and is the original source of a statement of fact or a logical assertion (or a collection of such facts and/or assertions) that is to be found in the citing entity. This inverse object property is designed to be used to relate a cited entity to a separate abstract, summary or nanopublication based upon it.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is documented by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Information about the cited entity is documented by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: shares author with
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which each entity has at least one author in common with the other entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: critiques
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity critiques statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: The ideas presented in [X] are badly substantantiated.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited as metadata document by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited as being the container of metadata relating to the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: confirms
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity confirms facts, ideas or statements presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Our findings are similar to those published in [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: links to
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity provides a link, in the form of an HTTP Uniform Resource Locator (URL), to the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: The BioSharing registry (https://biosharing.org) can be of use as it describes the standards in detail, including versions where applicable.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: distant citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation in which the citing and the cited entities have nothing significant in common with one another (for example authors, journal, institutional affiliation, or funding agency) over and beyond their subject matter.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Derived from the article "A Small World of Citations? The Influence of Collaboration Networks on Citation Practices" by Matthew L. Wallace, Vincent Larivière and Yves Gingras, published in PLOS One (https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0033339).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: author self citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation in which the citing and the cited entities have at least one author in common.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Like the ancestor class `cito:Citation`, `cito:AuthorSelfCitation` and its accompanying object properties `cito:hasCitingEntity`, `cito:hasCitedEntity` and `cito:hasCitationCharacterization` can be employed to reify direct citation statements made using the CiTO citation object property `cito:cites` or one of its sub-properties, accompanied by an additional statement using `cito:sharesAuthorWith` for linking the citing paper and the cited paper.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: has citation time span
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The temporal characteristic of a citation, namely the interval between the publication date of the cited entity and the publication date of the citing entity. Note that when one or both of the publication dates is given as just "year", then the citation time span is rounded to the nearest year, and when one or both of the publication dates is given as just "year and month", then the citation time span is rounded to the nearest month, with the inherent inaccuracies that such rounding involves.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: shares funding agency with
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which two entities result from activities that have been funded by the same funding agency.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: provides quotation for
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity contains information, usually of a textual nature, that is quoted by (used as a quotation within) the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: reviews
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity reviews statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: This paper discusses Toulmin's methodology in modelling argumentation [X], focussing on highlighting advantages and drawbacks of the application of such a methodology in the Social Web.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: gives background to
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity provides background information for the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: compiles
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity is used to create or compile the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note:
Example: This book gathers interviews with academic researchers of several disciplines [X].
Note: This property has been imported from the CiTO4Data ontology, usage of which has been deprecated.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: journal cartel citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation from one journal to another journal which forms one of a very large number of citations from the citing journal to recent articles in the cited journal, possibly undertaken as part of a citation cartel for the purpose of gaming the impact factor of the cited journal.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Derived from the blog post "What do we know about journal citation cartels? A call for information" by Philippe Mongeon, Ludo Waltman and Sarah de Rijcke (https://www.cwts.nl/blog?article=n-q2w2b4).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is disputed by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents statements, ideas or conclusions that are disputed by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: has co-authorship citation level
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The minimal distance that one of the authors of the citing entity has with regards to one of the authors of the cited entity, according to their co-authorship network.
rdf:Description.skos:note: For instance, a citation has a co-authorship citation level equal to 1 if at least one author of the citing entity has previously published as co-author with one of the authors of the cited entity. Similarly, we say that a citation has a co-authorship citation level equal to 2 if at least one author of the citing entity has previously published as co-author with someone who him/herself has previously published as co-author with one of the authors of the cited entity. And so on.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: author network self citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation in which at least one author of the citing entity has direct or indirect co-authorship links with one of the authors of the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Derived from the article "A Small World of Citations? The Influence of Collaboration Networks on Citation Practices" by Matthew L. Wallace, Vincent Larivière and Yves Gingras, published in PLOS One (https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0033339).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: replies to
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity replies to statements, ideas or criticisms presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We will not investigate the issues of the approach proposed in [X] here, but rather we introduce yet another alternative.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: gives support to
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity provides intellectual or factual support for the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is updated by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents statements, ideas, hypotheses or understanding that are updated by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: supports
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity provides intellectual or factual support for statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We support Galileo's statement [X], that Earth moves.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is refuted by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents statements, ideas or conclusions that are refuted by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: retracts
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity constitutes a formal retraction of the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We wrote that the Earth moves in [X]; we now retire such statement.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: funder self citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation in which the works reported in the citing and the cited entities were funded by the same funding agency.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Like the ancestor class `cito:Citation`, `cito:FunderSelfCitation` and its accompanying object properties `cito:hasCitingEntity`, `cito:hasCitedEntity` and `cito:hasCitationCharacterization` can be employed to reify direct citation statements made using the CiTO citation object property `cito:cites` or one of its sub-properties, accompanied by an additional statement using `cito:sharesFundingAgencyWith` for linking the citing paper and the cited paper.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: shares journal with
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing and cited bibliographic resources are published in the same journal.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is compiled by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is the result of a compile or creation event using the citing entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Note: This property has been imported from the CiTO4Data ontology, usage of which has been deprecated.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited as potential solution by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited as providing or containing a possible solution to the issues being discussed in the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: disagrees with
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity disagrees with statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We do not share Galileo's opinion [X]: the Earth does not move.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is corrected by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents statements, ideas or conclusions that are corrected by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: disputes
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity disputes statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We doubt that Galileo is right when he writes [X] that the Earth moves.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: uses data from
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity describes work that uses data presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Using the information collected from our recent study [X], we can estimate that there are tens of millions of HTML forms with potentially useful deep-web content.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited as recommended reading by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited by the citing entity as an item of recommended reading.
rdf:Description.skos:note: This property can be used, for example, to describe references in a lecture reading list, where the cited references are relevant to the general topic of the lecture, but might not be individually cited within the text of the lecture. Similarly, it could be used to describe items in a "Suggested further reading" list at the end of a book chapter.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which a citing entity cites a cited entity, either directly and explicitly (as in the reference list of a journal article), indirectly (e.g. by citing a more recent paper by the same group on the same topic), or implicitly (e.g. as in artistic quotations or parodies, or in cases of plagiarism).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites as recommended reading
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity cites the cited entity as an item of recommended reading.
rdf:Description.skos:note:
Example: To our knowledge, [X] is the best source of exercises about UML, making it a valuable proposal for beginners.
This property can be used, for example, to describe references in a lecture reading list, where the cited references are relevant to the general topic of the lecture, but might not be individually cited within the text of the lecture. Similarly, it could be used to describe items in a "Suggested further reading" list at the end of a book chapter.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: shares publication venue with
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing and cited bibliographic resources are published in same publication venue.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is reviewed by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents statements, ideas or conclusions that are reviewed by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: includes excerpt from
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity includes one or more excerpts from the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note:
An excerpt is more general than a quotation. It is generally used to indicate a re-published extract from a book, instruction manual, film, radio programme, etc, that need not be what someone said. For example:
Oxford 01865 Oxshott 01372 Oxted 01883 Oxton 01578
is an excerpt from the UK Dialling Codes section of the Oxford Telephone Directory.
Example: In her work, the author states that even though most Human Information Behaviour researchers are familiar with the literature related to their studies, it is not uncommon for investigators to fail to see the benefits they may gain from previous mistakes [X]

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation is a conceptual directional link from a citing entity to a cited entity, created by a human performative act of making a citation, typically instantiated by the inclusion of a bibliographic reference (biro:BibliographicReference) in the reference list of the citing entity, or by the inclusion within the citing entity of a link, in the form of an HTTP Uniform Resource Locator (URL), to a resource on the World Wide Web.
rdf:Description.skos:note:
The time span of a citation, i.e. the interval between the publication year of the citing entity and the publication year of the cited entity, can be recorded using the data property `cito:hasCitationTimeSpan`.
The nature or type of a citation can be characterized by using CiTO object properties, e.g. http://purl.org/spar/cito/citesAsDataSource (definition: “The citing entity cites the cited entity as a source of data”).
This CiTO class `cito:Citation` and its accompanying object properties `cito:hasCitingEntity`, `cito:hasCitedEntity` and `cito:hasCitationCharacterization` can be employed to reify direct citation statements made using the CiTO citation object property `cito:cites` or one of its sub-properties.
This usage involved [OWL2 punning](http://www.w3.org/TR/2009/WD-owl2-new-features-20090611/#F12:_Punning), whereby a CiTO object property, such as the aforementioned `cito:extends`, is used as the object of the OWL assertion.
Using punning, the CiTO object property is considered as a proper named individual of the class `owl:Thing`.
Such reification of citation acts can be very useful, since it permits one to combine these CiTO properties with other vocabularies, or to handle situations in which none of the citation characterizations available in CiTO are applicable.
Such situations can be resolved by the creation of a user-defined citation characterization, for example by using the [Web Annotation Data Model](https://www.w3.org/TR/annotation-model/), as explained at http://semanticpublishing.wordpress.com/2013/07/03/extending-cito-for-open-annotations/.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: describes
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity describes the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Galileo's book [X] is a dialog among three scientists about Copernicus' eliocentric theory.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites as evidence
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity cites the cited entity as source of factual evidence for statements it contains.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We found an unquestionable demonstration of our hypothesis in [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited as authority by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited as providing an authoritative description or definition of the subject under discussion in the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: shares author institution with
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which each entity has at least one author that shares a common institutional affiliation with an author of the other entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is parodied by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The characteristic style or content of the cited entity is imitated by the citing entity for comic effect, usually without explicit citation.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: plagiarizes
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A property indicating that the author of the citing entity plagiarizes the cited entity, by including textual or other elements from the cited entity without formal acknowledgement of their source. The citing entity thus contains no explicit citation of the cited entity, according to the norms of scholarly practice, but cites it implicitly.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: The conclusion of our dissertation can be summarised by the following motto, we created specifically for this purpose: we are like dwarfs standing on the shoulders of giants.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is critiqued by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents statements, ideas or conclusions that are critiqued by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: likes
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity shows appreciation of or interest in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: This property enables social media "likes" statements to be encoded in RDF. Use of this property does NOT imply the existence of a formal citation of the entity that is "liked".

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is retracted by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is formally retracted by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is speculated on by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited because the citing article contains speculations on its content or ideas.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites as authority
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity cites the cited entity as one that provides an authoritative description or definition of the subject under discussion.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Newton asserted that we are like dwarfs standing on the shoulders of giants [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: provides method for
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity details a method that is used in work described by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is derided by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity contains ideas or conclusions for which the citing entity express derision.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites as data source
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity cites the cited entity as source of data.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Italy has more than ten thousand kilometers of shoreline: see [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited as data source by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited as a data source by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: citation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A citation or reference to another creative work, such as another publication, web page, scholarly article, etc.
rdf:Description.skos:note: This property is defined in [schema.org](https://schema.org/) and has been added here to align schema.org with CiTO. The object property `schema:citation` expresses similar semantics to `cito:cites` except for the explicit definition of domain and range classes, that are `schema:CreativeWork` according to schema.org. For that reason, it is here defined as a subproperty of `cito:cites`.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is linked to by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is the target for an HTTP Uniform Resource Locator (URL) link within the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is cited by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is cited by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is ridiculed by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity or aspects of its contents are ridiculed by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is agreed with by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity contains statements, ideas or conclusions with which the citing entity agrees.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is disagreed with by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity presents statements, ideas or conclusions that are disagreed with by the citing entity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: refutes
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity refutes statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We do not think that all their arguments in favour of their own and against the other strategies are equally convincing [X].

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cites as metadata document
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity cites the cited entity as being the container of metadata describing the citing entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: Basic bibliographic, entity and project metadata relating to this article, recorded in a structured machine-readable form, is available as an additional file [X] accompanying this paper.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: corrects
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity corrects statements, ideas or conclusions presented in the cited entity.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: The result published in [X] is partially wrong, the correct result is 42.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: speculates on
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the citing entity speculates on something within or related to the cited entity, without firm evidence.
rdf:Description.skos:note: Example: We believe that if Galileo believed that Earth goes around the Sun [X], he also should believe that Moon goes around Earth.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: is plagiarized by
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relation according to which the cited entity is plagiarized by the author of the citing entity, who includes within the citing entity textual or other elements from the cited entity without formal acknowledgement of their source. The cited entity is thus not explicitly cited from within the citing entity, according to the norms of scholarly practice, but is cited implicitly.
